rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anticipated excuse is that their forefathers committed shirk before them and their descendants merely followed their forebears and their guidance.
rows.anchor: من بعدهم } ، فاقتدينا بهم وبهداهم، لئلا تقولوا: { أفتهلكنا بما فعل المبطلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The appeal about punishment means, Will You punish us for what the falsifiers did? The falsifiers are their ancestors who denied God's oneness.
rows.anchor: يعني أفتعذبنا بما فعل المبطلون، يعني المكذبين بالتوحيد، يعنون آباءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sorted Adam's descendants as by lots: the white were promised Paradise by His mercy and the right side, while the black were assigned the Fire and the left side.
rows.anchor: ثم أفاضهم إفاضة القدح، فقال للبيض: هؤلاء في الجنة برحمتي، فهم أصحاب اليمين، وأصحاب الميمنة، وقال للسود: هؤلاء للنار، ولا أبالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God returned them all to Adam's loins; the dead remain in their graves until the covenant people emerge from men's loins and women's wombs and the Resurrection comes, when God counts them all.
rows.anchor: ثم أعادهم جميعا في صلب آدم، عليه السلام، فأهل القبور محبسون حتى يخرج الله أهل الميثاق كلهم من أصلاب الرجال وأرحام النساء، ثم تقوم الساعة، فذلك قوله: لقد أحصاهم يوم القيامة وعدهم عدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children who die young enter Paradise through knowing their Lord; those who reach maturity receive the covenant through knowing and obeying Him.
rows.anchor: فمن مات منهم صغيرا، فله الجنة بمعرفته بربه، ومن بلغ منهم العقل أخذ أيضا ميثاقه بمعرفته لربه، والطاعة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those who fail to believe on reaching maturity, the first covenant is no benefit; that original pledge stands as evidence against them.
rows.anchor: فمن لم يؤمن إذا بلغ العقل لم يغن عنه الميثاق الأول شيئا، وكان العهد والميثاق الأول حجة عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that most had no covenant means they failed to keep faith, and refers to most of Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: وما وجدنا لأكثرهم من عهد يعنى من وفاء، يعني أكثر ولد آدم، عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāsiqūn here means disobedient sinners among Adam's descendants.
rows.anchor: أكثرهم لفاسقين [الأعراف: 102]، يعني لعاصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explaining the signs here means making the covenant matter clear, so that people may return through repentance.
rows.anchor: يعني هكذا نبين الآيات في أمر الميثاق، { ولعلهم } ، يعني لكى { يرجعون } [آية: 174] إلى التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those whom God guides to His religion are rightly guided; those He leads away from it are the losers, referring here to the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: لدينه، { فهو المهتدي ومن يضلل } عن دينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hearts, eyes, and ears of these people fail to receive faith because God has sealed them, as in the verse about sealed hearts, hearing, and sight.
rows.anchor: ختم الله على قلوبهم وعلى سمعهم وعلى أبصارهم غشاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They resemble cattle because they eat and drink without attending to the Hereafter; cattle care only for eating, drinking, and mating, and the disbelievers are like them.
rows.anchor: يأكلون ويشربون ولا يلتفتون إلى الآخرة، كما تأكل الأنعام، ليس للأنعام همة غير الأكل والشرب والسفاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people meant are Meccan disbelievers, who are further astray from the way than cattle.
rows.anchor: يعني كفار مكة { أضل } ، يعني أضل سبيلا، يعني الطريق من الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cattle know and remember their Lord, but these people neither know their Lord nor affirm His oneness; that is why they are heedless.
rows.anchor: لأن الأنعام تعرف ربها وتذكره، وهم لا يعرفون ربهم ولا يوحدونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A man prayed invoking both Allah and al-Rahman, and Abu Jahl objected that Muhammad's followers claimed one Lord but invoked two; the verse about God's beautiful names was revealed.
rows.anchor: ودعا الرحمن، فقال رجل من مشركى مكة، وهو أبو جهل: أليس يزعم محمد وأصحابه أنهم يعبدون ربا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's beautiful names include al-Rahman, al-Rahim, al-Malik, al-Quddus, al-Salam, al-Mu'min, al-Muhaymin, al-Aziz, al-Jabbar, and al-Mutakabbir, among others.
rows.anchor: يعني الرحمن، الرحيم، الملك، القدوس، السلام، المؤمن، المهيمن، العزيز، الجبار، المتكبر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told the man to invoke Allah and al-Rahman, explaining that whichever of these names he invoked belonged to the possessor of the beautiful names.
rows.anchor: ادع الله، وادع الرحمن، ورغما لأنف المشركين، فإنك ما دعوت من هذه الأسماء، فله الأسماء الحسنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who incline from the truth give idols God's names, including al-Lat, al-Uzza, Hubal, Asaf, and Na'ila; God forbade naming idols with His name.
rows.anchor: في أسمائه عن الحق، فيسمون الآلهة: اللات، والعزى، وهبل، ونحوها، وأساف، ونائلة، فمنعهم الله أن يسموا شيئا من آلهتهم باسم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will repay those who distort His names with punishment in the Hereafter for what they did.
rows.anchor: { سيجزون } بالعذاب في الآخرة { ما كانوا يعملون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural angels who take the disbelievers' souls means the Angel of Death alone; he strikes their faces and backs in this world.
rows.anchor: يعني ملك الموت وحده، { يضربون وجوههم وأدبارهم } فى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the account resumes at the Resurrection, they enter Hell and its keepers tell them to taste the blazing punishment.
rows.anchor: ثم انقطع الكلام، فلما كان يوم القيامة دخلوا النار، تقول لهم خزنة جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is for their prior disbelief and denial, so God is not unjust: He does not punish them without a sin.
rows.anchor: يقول: ليس يعذبهم على غير ذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with Pharaoh's people means people like them in denial, and the earlier nations include Noah, 'Ad, Thamud, Abraham, and Shu'ayb's people.
rows.anchor: أي من قبل فرعون وقومه من الأمم الخالية، قوم نوح، وعاد، وثمود، وإبراهيم، وقوم شعيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelieving in God's signs means denying that His punishment would come in this world; He seized and destroyed them for disbelief and denial.
rows.anchor: يعني بعذاب الله بأنه ليس بنازل بهم فى الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is powerful in carrying out His will when He punishes and severe in punishment whenever He exacts it.
rows.anchor: في أمره حين عذبهم، { شديد العقاب } [آية: 52] إذا عاقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For Mecca's people, the blessing was relief from hunger and fear and the sending of Muhammad; they changed it by failing to recognize its Lord, so God changed their condition.
rows.anchor: على أهل مكة، أطعمهم من جوع، وآمنهم من خوف، ثم بعث فيهم محمدا رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فهذه النعمة التى غيروها، فلم يعرفوا ربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Pharaoh analogy applies to his people being destroyed at Badr and to the nations before Pharaoh, all of whom were destroyed.
rows.anchor: يعنى كأشباه { آل فرعون } وقومه فى الهلاك ببدر، { والذين من قبلهم } ، يعني الذين قبل آل فرعون من الأمم الخالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied their Lord's signs by denying that punishment would descend in this world.
rows.anchor: يعني بعذاب ربهم فى الدنيا بأنه غير نازل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God punished them for their sins, disbelief, and denial, drowning Pharaoh's people and the other nations; their wrongdoing means their polytheism.
rows.anchor: يقول: فعذبناهم بذنوبهم فى الدنيا وبكفرهم وبتكذيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger came to Mecca's people from among themselves, someone they knew and could not deny.
rows.anchor: يا أهل مكة { رسول من أنفسكم } تعرفونه ولا تنكرونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What grieves the Messenger is the sin they commit in their religion.
rows.anchor: يعز عليه ما أثمتم في دينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He is eager for them to find right guidance.
rows.anchor: { حريص عليكم } بالرشد والهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His compassion means tenderness and mercy toward believers, including loving affection; the verse about believers being merciful among themselves means they love one another.
rows.anchor: كقوله: الرأفة، يعني الرقة والرحمة، يعني مودة بعضكم لبعض، كقوله: رحمآء بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Paradise, سبحانك اللهم is a signal between the people and their servants when they want food or drink.
rows.anchor: فهذا علم بين أهل الجنة وبين الخدم إذا أرادوا الطعام والشراب دعواهم أن يقولوا في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tables arrive in immense abundance, with pearl legs, and servants bring seventy thousand golden dishes through four thousand doors.
rows.anchor: فإذا الموائد قد جاءت، فوضعت ميلا في ميل، قوائمها اللؤلؤ، ودخل عليهم الخدم من أربعة آلاف باب معهم صحاف الذهب سبعون ألف صحفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each dish contains a unique food; satisfaction opens a thousand further desires, and a drink digests what came before over forty years.
rows.anchor: في كل صحفة لون من الطعام ليس في صاحبتها مثله، كلما شبع ألقى الله عليه ألف باب من الشهوة، كلما شبع أتى بشربة تهضم ما قبلها بمقدار أربعين عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fruit is served, and birds like camels gleam with differently colored beaks, wings, backs, undersides, and legs.
rows.anchor: ويؤتون بألوان الثمار، وتجيء الطير أمثال البخت، مناقيرها لون، وأجنحتها لون، ظهورها لون، وبطونها لون، وقوائمها لون، تتلألأ نورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The couches are woven with ruby and fresh emerald rods, softer than silk, with pearl legs and gold and silver edges.
rows.anchor: في غرفة فيها سرر موضونة، والوضن مشبك وسطه بقضبان الياقوت والزمرد الرطب، ألين من الحرير، قوائمها اللؤلؤ، حافتاه ذهب وفضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The furnishings equal seventy rooms in an earthly house, and a person falling from that room would take seventy years to reach the earth's bottom.
rows.anchor: عليه من الفرش مقدار سبعين غرفة في دار الدنيا، لو أن رجلا وقع من تلك الغرفة لم يبلغ قرار الأرض سبعين عاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bird tells the blessed person where it grazed and drank; a chosen bird alights on the table in seventy thousand colors, half dried and half roasted, then returns because no one dies in Paradise.
rows.anchor: يا ولي الله، رعيت في روضة كذا وكذا، وشربت من عين كذا وكذا، فأيتهن أعجبه وصفها وقعت على مائدته نصفها قديد سبعون ألف لون من الطير الواحد، والنصف شواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A messenger angel waits for the chamberlain's permission, then tells the blessed person that the Lord sends him peace.
rows.anchor: فلا يصل إليه حتى يستأذن له حاجب فيقوم بين يديه، فيقول: يا ولي الله، ربك يقرأ عليك السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After finishing their food and drink, the people of Paradise say praise belongs to God, Lord of all worlds.
rows.anchor: فإذا فرغوا من الطعام والشراب، قالوا: الحمد لله رب العالمين، وذلك قوله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The humiliating punishment promised is drowning, while the abiding punishment is the lasting punishment of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: يعني يذله، يعني الغرق، { ويحل عليه } ، ويجب عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The coming of God's command means His word that punishment will descend; the oven gushed water from the oven in Noah's farthest house in Syria, at Ayn Warda.
rows.anchor: يعني قولنا في نزول العذاب بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairs are two kinds, male and female; without the word two, the dual phrase could imply four.
rows.anchor: يعني صنفين اثنين ذكرا وأنثى، فهو زوجان، ولولا أنه قال: اثنين، لكان الزوجان أربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's family included his wife Wāliga and Lot's wife Wāhila; the excluded family member was the son Canaan, whose punishment was decreed in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: واسمها والغة، واسم امرأة لوط والهة، في السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believed in God's oneness were to be carried in the ship.
rows.anchor: يعني ومن صدق بتوحيد الله، فاحمله في السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The few with Noah numbered eighty: forty men and forty women; the village called Eighty lies in the Jazira near Mosul, at Bafarda.
rows.anchor: يقال: بأنهم أربعون رجلا وأربعون امرأة عددهم ثمانون نفسا، واسم القرية اليوم قرية الثمانين، وهي بالجزيرة قريبة من الموصل، وهي بافردى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' signs were the hand and the staff.
rows.anchor: يعني اليد والعصى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's notables means the elite of his people; they obeyed his command to accept his view, as in the verse where he says he shows them only what he sees.
rows.anchor: يعني أشراف قومه، { فاتبعوا أمر فرعون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's command was not rightly guided, meaning it did not guide them.
rows.anchor: { ومآ أمر فرعون برشيد } [آية: 97] لهم، يعني بهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh leads the Copts as their leader to the Fire at the Resurrection, and they follow him as they did in this world.
rows.anchor: القبط { يوم القيامة } ، يعني فرعون قائدهم إلى النار، ويتبعونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To bring them to the Fire means to enter them; the Fire is a dreadful place to enter.
rows.anchor: { فأوردهم النار } فأدخلهم، { وبئس الورد المورود } [آية: 98] المدخل المدخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The curse in this world is drowning; a second curse awaits them in the Fire at the Resurrection, and the two curses follow one another like successive gifts.
rows.anchor: يعني العذاب، وهو الغرق، { ويوم القيامة } لعنة أخرى في النار، { بئس الرفد المرفود } [آية: 99]، فكأن اللعنتين أردفت إحداهما الأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the unseen, including the descent of punishment and what is in the earth.
rows.anchor: يقول: ولله غيب نزول العذاب، وغيب ما في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servants' affairs return to God on the Resurrection, as in the verse saying all affairs return to God.
rows.anchor: يعني أمر العباد يرجع إلى الله يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship God alone and place your trust in Him, meaning rely on God.
rows.anchor: يعني وحده، { وتوكل عليه } ، يقول: وثق بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the Lord is not unaware of their deeds is a threat.
rows.anchor: { وما ربك بغافل عما تعملون } [آية: 123]، هذا وعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God regards secret and public speech equally; the person hidden in sin at night spreads that same sin openly by day, and God knows it all.
rows.anchor: يقول: من هو مستخف بالمعصية في ظلمة الليل، ومنتشر بتلك المعصية بالنهار معلن بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels before and behind a person protect him, by God's command, from humans and jinn until destiny allows harm; if God changes his condition, the angels cannot help.
rows.anchor: يعني بأمر الله من الإنس والجن مما لم يقدر أن يصيبه حتى تسلمه المقادير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God changes a people's blessing only after they change themselves; this refers to Meccan disbelievers and parallels the account in al-Anfal.
rows.anchor: يعني كفار مكة، نظيرها من الأنفال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing was the Messenger sent from among them, food after hunger, and safety after fear; they changed it, so God changed their situation.
rows.anchor: والنعمة أنه بعث فيهم رسولا من أنفسهم، وأطعمهم من جوع، وآمنهم من خوف، فغيروا هذه النعمة، فغير الله ما بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil God wills means punishment; nothing can turn it away, and no protector besides God can repel it.
rows.anchor: يعني بالسوء العذاب، { فلا مرد له وما لهم من دونه من وال }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad was sent to the Meccans, after earlier nations had passed, to recite the Qur'an revealed to him.
rows.anchor: يعني هكذا { أرسلناك في أمة قد خلت من قبلها أمم } ، يعني قد مضت قبل أهل مكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Hudaybiya, Suhayl ibn Amr rejected the basmala with al-Rahman, saying he knew that name only for Musaylima, and asked Ali to write باسمك اللهم instead.
rows.anchor: فقال سهيل بن عمرو القرشي: ما نعرف الرحمن إلا مسيلمة، ولكن اكتب: باسمك اللهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Suhayl's group refused the title Messenger of God and demanded Muhammad ibn Abd Allah; the Companions wanted to fight, but the Prophet told Ali to write what they wanted and promised a similar day would come.
rows.anchor: فقالوا: ما نعرف أنك رسول الله، لقد ظلمناك إذا إن كنت رسول الله، ثم نمنعك عن دخول المسجد الحرام، ولكن اكتب: هذا ما صالح عليه محمد بن عبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truce stipulated that Muhammad leave that year and return the next to perform the minor pilgrimage, while Mecca's people left the city to him for three nights.
rows.anchor: على أن ينصرف محمد من عامه هذا، فإذا كان القابل دخل مكة، فقضى عمرته وخلى أهل مكة بينه وبين مكة ثلاث ليال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation about denying al-Rahman concerns Quraysh leaders Suhayl, Makraz ibn Hafs ibn al-Ahnaf, and Huwaytib ibn Abd al-Uzza.
rows.anchor: في قول سهيل وصاحبيه مكرز بن حفص بن الأحنف، وحويطب بن عبد العزى، كلهم من قريش حين قالوا: ما نعرف الرحمن، إلا مسيلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is to say that the al-Rahman whom they deny is his Lord and that there is no deity except Him.
rows.anchor: الرحمن الذى يكفرون به هو ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trusting God means relying on Him; returning to Him means repentance, as in the parallel verse in al-Furqan.
rows.anchor: يقول: به أثق، { وإليه متاب } [آية: 30]، يعني التوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' signs were the hand and staff, and bringing Israel from darkness to light means calling them from polytheism to faith.
rows.anchor: اليد والعصا، { أن أخرج قومك } ، يعني أن ادع قومك بنى إسرائيل، { من الظلمات إلى النور } ، يعني من الشرك إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminding them of God's days means warning them with examples of earlier nations' punishment so they will take heed and believe.
rows.anchor: عظهم وخوفهم بمثل عذاب الأمم الخالية، فيحذروا فيؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction of past nations teaches every patient and grateful believer: the believer endures severe trials and gives thanks for God's blessings.
rows.anchor: يعني لعبرة { لكل صبار شكور } [آية: 5]، يعني المؤمن صبور على أمر الله عز وجل عند البلاء الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites were rescued from Pharaoh's people in Egypt, who tortured them severely by killing their sons and sparing their daughters; Pharaoh killed eighteen of their children.
rows.anchor: ثم بين العذاب، فقال: { ويذبحون أبناءكم } ، في حجور أمهاتهم، { ويستحيون نساءكم } ، يعني قتل البنين وترك البنات، قتل فرعون منهم ثمانية عشر طفلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great bala' from God here means punishment or affliction; in the cited verses, the phrase manifest bala' means a clear blessing.
rows.anchor: { بلاء } ، يعني نقمة، { من ربكم عظيم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis asks for respite until people are raised after death, meaning until the second blast; the analogy about waiting until ease means granting a delay.
rows.anchor: يعني يبعث الناس بعد الموت، يقول: أجلنى إلى يوم النفخة الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis is granted life until the appointed term, the first blast; he had wanted to survive until the Resurrection because he knew no one dies after being raised.
rows.anchor: إلى أجل موقوت، وهي النفخة الأولى، وإنما أراد عدو الله الأجل إلى يوم يبعثون؛ لئلا يذوق الموت؛ لأنه قد علم أنه لا يموت بعد البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblis says that because God led him astray, he will beautify earthly life for people and lead them away from guidance.
rows.anchor: يقول: أما إذا أضللتني، { لأزينن لهم في الأرض ولأغوينهم أجمعين } [آية: 39]، يعني ولأضلنهم عن الهدى أجمعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sincere servants are people of tawhid whom God has chosen for His religion; Iblis knows he has no authority over them.
rows.anchor: يعني أهل التوحيد، وقد علم إبليس أن الله استخلص عبادا لدينه، ليس له عليهم سلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The linked verse says Satan has no authority over God's servants; their Lord serves as their safeguard and barrier.
rows.anchor:
يعني مالك أن تضلهم عن الهدى، وكفى بربك وكيلا
[الإسراء: 65]، يعني حرزا ومانعا لعباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path to God means the path of truth and guidance; here على means for, as in the verse about witnesses for people and the verse about the Lord's straight path.
rows.anchor: يقول: هذا طريق الحق الهدى إلى، { مستقيم } [آية: 41]، يعني الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan has no power over God's servants except those who follow him among the misguided.
rows.anchor: إلا من اتبعك من الغاوين } [آية: 42]، يعني من المضلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell is the appointed place for the disbelieving jinn and humans, Iblis, and his descendants.
rows.anchor: يعني كفار الجن والإنس، وإبليس وذريته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell has seven gates, one below another and each hotter by seventy degrees than the one above, with seventy years between adjacent gates; their names are Jahannam, Laza, Hutama, Sa'ir, Jahim, Hawiya, and Saqar.
rows.anchor: بعضها أسفل من بعض، كل باب أشد حرا من الذي فوقه بسبعين جزءا، بين كل بابين سبعين سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each gate contains a known number of disbelieving jinn and humans, and the second gate's punishment is seventy times more severe than the first's.
rows.anchor: يعني عدد معلوم من كفار الجن والإنس، يعني الباب الثانى يضعف على الباب الأول في شدة العذاب سبعين ضعفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God overturned the four cities and rained clay-mixed stones on Sodom, Damura, Amura, and Sabura and people outside the towns; a stone could reach someone elsewhere and kill him.
rows.anchor: { فجعلنا } المدائن الأربع { عاليها سافلها وأمطرنا عليهم } سدوم، ودامورا، وعامورا وصابورا، وأمطرنا على من كان خارجا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sijjil means stones mixed with clay.
rows.anchor: { من سجيل } ، يعني الحجارة خلطها الطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction of Lot's people is a lesson for later observers, who should beware receiving a like punishment.
rows.anchor: يقول: للناظرين من بعدهم، فيحذرون مثل عقوبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's ruined towns lie on a clear, enduring route between Mecca and Syria that Meccans and others travel.
rows.anchor: قرى لوط التى أهلكت بطريق مستقيم، يعني واضح مقيم يمر عليها أهل مكة وغيرهم، وهي بين مكة والشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction is a sign for believers after them to avoid the same punishment, and warns Meccan disbelievers with the fate of earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: يعني للمصدقين بتوحيد الله عز وجل لمن بعدهم، فيحذرون عقوبتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Horses, mules, and donkeys are for riding and adornment, meaning a handsome appearance; God also creates creatures people do not know, as in the verse about someone appearing in his finery.
rows.anchor: يقول: لكم في ركوبها جمال وزينة، يعني الشارة الحسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes the straight path clear as guidance; other paths turn away from guidance, and had He willed, He would have guided everyone to His religion.
rows.anchor: يعني بيان الهدى، { ومنها جآئر } ، يقول: ومن السبيل ما تكون جائرة على الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain provides drinking water and trees where livestock graze.
rows.anchor: يعني المطر لكم منه شراب، { ومنه شجر فيه تسيمون } [آية: 10]، يعني وفيه ترعون أنعامكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain grows grain, olives, dates, grapes, and every kind of fruit as a sign for people to reflect on God's oneness.
rows.anchor: بالمطر، { الزرع والزيتون والنخيل والأعناب ومن كل الثمرات إن في ذلك لآية } ، فيما ذكر لكم من النبات لعبرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the sea serve people so they can eat fresh fish, take pearls for jewelry, sail ships back and forth in one wind, seek His bounty, and give thanks.
rows.anchor: وهو السمك ما أصيد أو ألقاه الماء وهو حي، { وتستخرجوا منه حلية تلبسونها } ، يعني اللؤلؤ، { وترى الفلك } ، يعني السفن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God set mountains in the earth to keep it from moving and swaying its inhabitants, and provided flowing rivers and roads so people can find their way.
rows.anchor: يعني الجبال، { أن تميد بكم } ، يعني لئلا تزول بكم الأرض فتميل بمن عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are mountains, as in the cited comparison to mountain-like landmarks.
rows.anchor:
يعني الجبال، كقوله سبحانه:
كالأعلام
[الرحمن: 14]، يعني الجبال

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The stars used for navigation are Banat Na'sh, al-Jady, the two Farqads, and al-Qutb; they stay fixed year-round and, together with mountains, help travelers navigate land and sea.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: هي بنات نعش، والجدي، والفرقدان، والقطب، قال: بعينها لأنهن لا يزلن عن أماكنهن شتاء ولا صيفا، يعني بالجبال، والكواكب، وبها يعرفون الطرق في البر والبحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People find their way by the stars, while the linked phrase about not finding a path means not knowing the way.
rows.anchor:
لا يهتدون سبيلا
[النساء: 98]، يعني لا يعرفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Creator of all the preceding things is unlike idols such as al-Lat, al-Uzza, Manat, and Hubal, which create nothing; people should reflect and affirm God's oneness.
rows.anchor: هذه الأشياء من أول السورة إلى هذه الآية، { كمن لا يخلق } شيئا من الآلهة: اللات، والعزى، ومناة، وهبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Muslim invoked Allah and al-Rahman in prayer, and a pagan mocked the claim of one Lord; God then revealed the prohibition on taking two gods.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن رجلا من المسلمين دعا الله عز وجل في صلاته، ودعا الرحمن، فقال رجل من المشركين: أليس يزعم محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه أنهم يعبدون ربا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To fear God here means fearing Him by abandoning tawhid; whoever does not affirm His oneness has the Fire.
rows.anchor: يعني إياي فخافون في ترك التوحيد فمن لم يوحد فله النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything in the heavens and earth belongs to God as His creatures and property; His religion is everlasting Islam, and the question asks whether people worship anyone but Him.
rows.anchor: من الخلق عبيده وفي ملكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham was an ummah, a teacher and an exemplary leader in good; he was obedient and devoted, and not a polytheist, meaning neither Jew nor Christian.
rows.anchor: يعني معلما، يعني إماما يقتدى به في الخير، { قانتا } مطيعا { لله حنيفا } ، يعني مخلصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham thanked God for His favors; God chose him for prophethood and guided him to the straight religion of Islam.
rows.anchor: يعني لأنعم الله عز وجل: { اجتباه } ، يعني استخلصه للرسالة والنبوة، { وهداه إلى صراط مستقيم } [آية: 121]، يعني إلى دين مستقيم، وهو الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham's worldly good was a favorable reputation for obeying and patiently pleasing God, including enduring the fire, breaking idols, and intending to sacrifice Ishaq; all religious communities praise and claim him, and he is righteous in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: وأعطينا إبراهيم في الدنيا مقالة حسنة بمضيته وصبره على رضا ربه عز وجل، حين ألقي في النار، وكسر الأصنام، وأراد ذبح ابنه إسحاق، والثناء الحسن من أهل الأديان كلها يتولونه جميعا، ولا يتبرأ منه أحد منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's establishment over the Throne means that He settled there before creating the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: في التقديم قبل خلق السموات والأرض يعني استقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything above, below, and between the heavens and earth belongs to God; under the lowest earth are the rock, king, bull, fish, water, and wind blowing in the air.
rows.anchor: يعني بالثرى الأرض السفلى وتحتها الصخرة والملك والثور والحوت والماء والريح تهب في الهواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what people say aloud, what they hide within themselves, and what they do without knowing that He knows it.
rows.anchor: يعني ما أسر العبد في نفسه { و } ما { وأخفى } [آية: 7] من السر، مالا يعلم أنه يعلمه، وهو عامله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone has the beautiful names, those listed at the end of al-Hashr and similar passages; this answers Meccan disbelievers who demanded proof there was no other god alongside Him.
rows.anchor: وهي التي في آخر سورة الحشر ونحوه، لقولهم: ائتنا ببراءة أنه ليس مع إلهك إله
